description: A clock multiplier with four independent rows and two clock inputs you can flip between, for stacking faster and faster pulse streams

params.text: Swaps the module between its two clock inputs
Makes every row fire on each beat of the chosen clock even where that row's gate is closed, while leaving the faster subdivisions to the open rows alone
How many pulses this row puts out for each beat of the chosen clock, a whole number from 1 to 8

inputs.text: A rising edge above 1V swaps the module between its two clock inputs
One of the two clock inputs, and the one in use when a patch is loaded; the interval between two rising edges above 1V is the tempo every output is worked out from
The second of the two clock inputs, brought into use by FLIP; the interval between two rising edges above 1V is then the tempo every output is worked out from
Runs this row while the voltage here is at or above 5V and stops it below that; with nothing patched the row runs

outputs.text: A 1ms pulse at this row's multiplied rate
A 1ms pulse at the first two rows' multipliers multiplied together, counting only rows whose gate is open
A 1ms pulse at the first three rows' multipliers multiplied together, counting only rows whose gate is open
A 1ms pulse at all four rows' multipliers multiplied together, counting only rows whose gate is open

notes: nothing comes out until a clock is patched and has ticked twice: the tempo is measured from the gap between two edges at whichever input is in use.
the multiplied beats stop once a whole clock interval has gone by with no new edge, so a clock that stops leaves the module silent rather than free-running.
flipping to the other clock keeps the tempo last measured there, so the rows carry on at the old rate until that clock ticks twice.
